record.summary: Eleven young men completed 12 weeks of knee-extension training. The study compared first-session T2 MRI activation measures with subsequent T1 MRI muscle-volume and cross-sectional-area changes. Distal rectus-femoris activation and growth exceeded proximal values, but activation differences between quadriceps muscles did not reproduce their growth differences. Activation here was MRI-based, not surface EMG.
record.title: Inter- and intramuscular differences in training-induced hypertrophy of the quadriceps femoris: association with muscle activation during the first training session

record.summary: Healthy young adults performed maximum isometric knee extensions with hip and knee at 60 degrees. Surface EMG from three quadriceps sites and medial/lateral hamstrings was recorded alongside dynamometer torque. Four extensions followed a flexion reference contraction; retesting was at least three days later. The co-activation index was nonzero, depended on processing, and was more repeatable within than between sessions. The abstract reports eight volunteers; Methods reports ten, five women and five men. This discrepancy is unresolved.
record.title: Quantifying thigh muscle co-activation during isometric knee extension contractions: Within- and between-session reliability

record.summary: Dunstan and colleagues studied 19 completers, 11 men and eight women aged 45-65 with overweight or obesity, in a randomized three-condition acute crossover with at least six days between conditions. Following a drink containing 75 g glucose and 50 g fat, five hours of uninterrupted sitting was compared with two-minute walking breaks every 20 minutes: light walking at 3.2 km/h or moderate walking at 5.8-6.4 km/h, totaling 14 bouts and 28 minutes. Walking-break conditions reduced positive five-hour glucose and insulin incremental area under the curve relative to uninterrupted sitting. These were acute metabolic measurements, not future health or function outcomes.
record.title: Acute walking breaks during prolonged sitting: glucose and insulin responses

record.summary: An anonymous online cross-sectional survey recruited through Facebook, associations and gyms in English-speaking countries. Eligibility covered women aged 20-89 competing in all three powerlifting lifts; analyzed respondents were aged 20-71. Of 778 responses, 154 incomplete, 142 not competing in all three lifts and two from respondents under 20 were excluded, leaving 480. Survey urinary incontinence used ISI greater than zero. Recent three-month incontinence was reported by 211/480 (43.9%). Leakage during maximum attempts was reported by 194/480 in training and 147/480 in competition; these are separate survey contexts, not rates per lift exposure.
record.title: Survey-reported urinary leakage in competitive women powerlifters
